body: Oreshika: Tainted Bloodlines is Alfa System's PlayStation Vita role-playing game, first released in Japan on 17 July 2014. A cursed family confronts demons while its members are limited to very short lives, making descendants essential to the campaign. The player develops a lineage rather than expecting one unchanged party to reach the end. Children inherit traits from their parents and continue the work after them. The structure makes time part of character development: a strong fighter is valuable now, but the future of the family depends on what can be passed on before that life ends.

Victories provide the means to form unions with deities and bring new children into the family. The player chooses names and classes, developing a group whose abilities must serve both the next expedition and the longer lineage. Dungeon encounters supply experience, equipment and techniques, while the mansion provides a central place to manage the family. A character's limited lifespan changes the meaning of investment. Training is still useful, but it belongs to an ongoing household whose strength must survive the departure of the particular person carrying it.

Shoji Masuda directed and designed the game, with Konosuke Kihara composing its music. The style draws on traditional Japanese artwork while three-dimensional faces make inherited resemblances visible. It follows an earlier PlayStation game without requiring direct knowledge of that story, placing the new family a century later. North American and European digital releases followed in March 2015. The campaign's distinctive achievement is to make succession playable, connecting the emotional loss of a developed character to the practical arrival of someone whose appearance and capabilities preserve part of the person who came before.

Prepare the next generation while fighting the present battle
A Japanese visual tradition shapes the family
